title: Tale of the Weaver Who Became a Leach

keywords: tale of the weaver who became a leach
full_text:
In Cairo lived an idle weaver named Abu Ali, who grew weary of his handloom. Seeing that the royal physician received hundred-dinar fees and rode a white mule caparisoned in velvet, Abu Ali threw away his shuttle, purchased a brass mortar, filled fifty glass vials with colored water and powdered chalk, and put up a sign: 'Master Physician of Ancient Sciences!'

His first patient was an elderly woman suffering from a common cold; Abu Ali prescribed warm chamomile tea and honey, and she recovered, spreading his fame!

Emboldened by accidental success, Abu Ali was summoned to the palace of the Grand Vizier to diagnose a mysterious ailment affecting the minister’s prize Arabian stallion.

Abu Ali examined the horse, pretended to read the stars, and declared with theatrical gravity: 'This stallion has a cold in his liver! He must be rubbed with hot mustard and fed thirty raw onions!'

The stallion ate the onions, sneezed with a mighty blast that knocked Abu Ali flat into the horse-trough, broke his halter, and galloped around the courtyard in a frenzy!

The chief royal veterinary surgeon arrived, examined the horse, and pulled a sharp thorn from the beast’s gum, instantly restoring the animal to peace.

The surgeon exposed Abu Ali’s fraudulent herbs before the entire court.

The vizier gave Abu Ali twenty lashes for his dangerous charlatanry and sent him back to his handloom, warning: 'Weave linen, fool, and leave medicine to those who have studied the anatomy of living creatures!'
moral: True medicine and science require disciplined study; ignorant pretension endangers human life.
